page.title: Best 8 Port KVM Switch (2026): 4K HDMI, Homelab and PiKVM Picks
page.desc: The best 8 port KVM switch for 4K 60 Hz desks, homelab racks with PiKVM, and 144 Hz gaming PCs, with the black-screen and EDID fixes owners need.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 8 port KVM switch is the TESmart HKS801-P23 ({buy:tesmart-hks801-p23}): 8 PCs to one HDMI monitor at 4K 60 Hz, USB 3.0 (5 Gb/s) sharing, an EDID emulator on every input, and RS232/LAN control. For a homelab rack on a budget, the TESmart HKS801-L23 ({buy:tesmart-hks801-l23}) switches the same 8 machines at 4K 30 Hz with USB 2.0, and PiKVM has a built-in driver that switches TESmart units over the network.

The top complaint is a black screen after switching. EDID emulators stop most of it on a desk. Behind a PiKVM capture box, though, 3 of 3 owners in one Techno Tim thread needed a fix: an EDID adapter, a cheap HDMI splitter, or removing the 4K emulators. TESmart's own advice is to power on the monitor first, then the KVM, then connect the PCs, and to keep the monitor cable under 5 m (16 ft) at 4K 60 Hz.

Do you want a power button for each server in a browser? Then a TESmart is the wrong tool. The PiKVM Switch gives each port its own EDID and ATX power control. It costs $274.95 per 4-port unit at PiShop.us (seen 2026-11-10, listed out of stock), so 8 servers need two units plus a PiKVM V4 Plus or V3. For 8 gaming or editing PCs on one high-refresh screen, the TESmart HKS801-M24 ({buy:tesmart-hks801-m24}) passes HDMI 2.1 at 4K 144 Hz with VRR.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Black screen or lost video after switching (5 reports): 3 owners in a Techno Tim PiKVM thread, 1 MT-VIKI owner on the GL.iNet forum, and 1 TESmart buyer on Trustpilot. Fixes that worked were an EDID adapter or HDMI splitter between the switch and the capture box, power-cycling the KVM, and connecting PCs after the KVM is on.
  • USB ports stop working while video still switches (6 users, several TESmart models): in one TESmart community thread. One fix was confirmed by a firmware update. Other users got replacements. Keep the receipt and register for the longer warranty.
  • Network control is clumsy to set up (3 sources): TESmart units ship at 192.168.1.10 with no DHCP. You change the address with a Windows utility, and the change only applies after a power cycle.
  • 4K 30 Hz versus 60 Hz confusion (3 listings): TESmart's HKS801-L23 and HKS801-EB23 titles say 4K 30 Hz while their descriptions say 60 Hz, and MT-VIKI listings disagree too. Plan on 4K 30 Hz for any 8-port switch that isn't sold as HDMI 2.0 or 2.1.
  • Smaller gripes: 1 to 2 second USB pauses after a switch, hotkeys that only work from the dedicated keyboard port, and 1.5 m (5 ft) included cables that are short for deep racks.

Which one by need

  • Desk or bench, 8 PCs on one 4K monitor: TESmart HKS801-P23 ({buy:tesmart-hks801-p23}). It runs 4K 60 Hz with USB 3.0 for shared drives. StarTech's R8AH202 also runs 4K 60 Hz and is sold mainly through business resellers.
  • Homelab rack, 1080p or 1440p, PiKVM in front: TESmart HKS801-L23 ({buy:tesmart-hks801-l23}). PiKVM's tesmart driver adds the 8 inputs to its Switches menu.
  • Remote power control for every server: PiKVM Switch. Each port has its own EDID and an ATX connector, but you need 2 units and a PiKVM for 8 machines.
  • 8 gaming or editing PCs at 4K 120 to 144 Hz: TESmart HKS801-M24 ({buy:tesmart-hks801-m24}).
  • Cheapest local 8-port, no network control: the MT-VIKI MT-801HK-C, sold on Amazon. It runs 4K 30 Hz with USB 2.0.

Not recommended

  • TESmart HKS801-EB23 ($229.00 on tesmart.com, 2026-11-10): it has the same 8 ports, USB 2.0 and 4K 30 Hz title as the HKS801-L23 at a higher price. TESmart says it uses an upgraded chip for compatibility, which is worth paying for only if the L23 sells out.
  • Any KVM for servers with IPMI, iDRAC or iLO: the built-in remote console already does the job.
  • 4K-rated EDID emulators in front of a PiKVM: one owner could only stream 640 × 480 until they were removed.

notes: Query choice: '8 port kvm switch'. The pages ranking for it now are store listings (StarTech, Dell, Adorama), reseller pages and dated SEO roundups, with no hands-on comparison. TESmart has the widest 8-port HDMI line, and PiKVM ships a built-in driver for TESmart LAN models. Pain points with counts: black screen or lost video after switching (5: 3 owners in the Techno Tim discussion, 1 MT-VIKI owner on the GL.iNet forum, 1 Trustpilot buyer); USB ports dying while video still works (6 users in one TESmart community thread, models HKS401-P23, HDC202-P23, HDC403-P23, HKS1601A1U and a 2-port kit, none of them the 8-port); network or RS232 setup clumsy (3: PiKVM docs, review-rating.com summary, Techno Tim); 4K 30 vs 60 Hz spec confusion (3 listings); USB re-enumeration pause of 1 to 2 s (2); hotkeys only from the dedicated port (2); short 1.5 m cables (2); weak IR remote (2). Segment winners: desk 4K60 with USB 3 goes to TESmart HKS801-P23; budget homelab or PiKVM front end goes to TESmart HKS801-L23; remote-first with per-server ATX power goes to the PiKVM Switch (not ours, named honestly); 4K144 gaming goes to TESmart HKS801-M24; cheapest local option without network control is MT-VIKI (Amazon-only, no price shown per the temporary rule). Verified 2026-11-10 with storecheck search on tesmart.com: P23 $399.00 in stock; L23 $143.99 (compare-at $239.99) in stock; M24 $599.00 in stock; EB23 $229.00 in stock. storecheck 'product' and WebFetch of the product pages returned HTTP 429 all session, so variant lists and the full spec tables were not read. The prices come from the store's own search feed, not snippets. Unverified and kept off the page: whether the P23 has a physical LAN port (the title says RS232/LAN, the description lists only RS232); M24 LAN control (the listing text and spec table conflict, so it is a caveat); exact count of shared USB 3.0 ports on the P23; StarTech R8AH202 price (about $700 per reseller snippets only) and its USB and EDID details; MT-VIKI specs (from reseller listings and manual snippets) and whether mt-viki.com is its official site (the footer company name matches, the domain was not confirmed); TESmart extended-warranty length (support pages say 2 and 3 years, the home banner says up to 5).
